The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Extensive dark brown/black necrosis at the leaf margins, especially upper-left
- Yellowing (chlorosis) in adjacent green areas
- Irregular necrotic patches, not concentric rings

This pattern is consistent with Late Blight or possibly Septoria. Let me view one reference image for Late Blight.

The Late Blight reference shows dark brown/black lesions spreading irregularly across the leaf with remaining green tissue — this matches well with the test image's dark necrotic margins and yellowing pattern.

The test image features:
- Irregular dark brown-to-black necrosis at leaf margins
- Chlorosis/yellowing in adjacent tissue
- No concentric rings (rules out Early Blight)
- No small discrete spots (rules out Septoria)
- Pattern consistent with Late Blight's spreading water-soaked lesions turning dark necrotic
